To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the broadband spectral energy distributions of Mrk 5 01 during two months of the 2008 MW campaign can be described by a one-zone synch rotron self-Compt on model, that the source was in a low state during this period, and that there is tentative evidence that the X-rays and VHE were correlated.
we detected a low state of the source with a tentative X-ray/VHE correlation, and that the broadband emission during the low state can be described by the one-zone synch rotron self-Compt on model.

the broadband spectral energy distributions (SEDs) of blazars during flaring and non-flaring states can be adequately described with the one-zone synchrotro n self-Compton (SSC) model, and that the correlation between the X-rays and VHE during non-flaring activity suggests that the same emission mechanisms are responsible for the broadband emission during both low and high VHE flaring states.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the broadband emission and variability of blazars.
the study of the broadband emission and the temporal variability of blazars, with a particular focus on the non-flaring states.
the characterization of the broadband gamma-ray emission of Mrk 500 during the non-fla ring state.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
during the 2008 observational campaign, the VHE energy range was "too low" to resolve substantial structural differences of the source in this period.
there are sufficient data from flaring and non-flaring states now to suggest that the one-zone SSC model is the valid description of the blazar emission during these different states.
there is no major evidence for an emission component dominating the source emission which is different during flaring and non-flaring activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the one-zone SSC model is adequate to describe the emission of Mrk 51 during non-flaring as well as flaring activity.
the statistical properties of the VHE emission are consistent with those of the X-ray emission during low-activity states.
the one-zone SSC model applies for the entire MW campaign.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the one-zone SSC model applies during both flaring and non-flaring activity, and that future studies during flaring activity should focus on obtaining extensive and complementary data during non-flaring activity to better constrain, and possibly test, the models.
the SSC process can reproduce all the observed broadband spectral energy distribution features of Mrk 50 1 during the two months the source was observed.
the one-zone SSC model, with the same physical components since 1996, remains a valid approach for describing the broad-band emission of this blazar.
